# Core Requirements for an Online Spreadsheet Data Workspace
A streamlined online spreadsheet application with an interface modeled after Google Sheets, covering workbook and worksheet management, spreadsheet data editing, formula calculation, sorting and filtering, data validation, and basic pivot analysis. Sharing and collaboration, version-history restoration, advanced visual styling, charts, macros, real-time collaborative cursors, and integrations with external office suites are outside the core scope.

- REQ-1 Workbook Access and Lifecycle
  Supports viewing, opening, creating, renaming, importing, and exporting workbooks within the application. The home page is the entry point for workbooks; successful open, create, and import operations all enter the same editor page, and subsequent operations may modify only the currently opened workbook. After a workbook is opened, created, or imported, the editor state shown in the browser must be a stable workbook state: visiting or refreshing that exact workbook state must open the same workbook rather than another workbook or a temporary blank page, and successful workbook modifications must remain available through that visible workbook state. After returning to the home page or reopening, the workbook name, last-updated time, worksheet order, and last active worksheet remain consistent. Worksheet tabs on the same editor page use the ARIA tab role, with the active tab indicated by aria-selected="true"; the active worksheet grid uses the ARIA grid role, has the accessible name "Worksheet grid", and exposes aria-multiselectable="true". Grid cells use the ARIA gridcell role with their cell coordinates as accessible names (for example, A1); the current cell and every cell within the currently selected rectangular region expose aria-selected="true", while cells outside the region expose aria-selected="false".
  - REQ-1-1 Workbook Navigation
    Supports viewing and opening available workbooks from the home page. After a workbook is successfully created, renamed, or imported from CSV, returning to or refreshing the home page must show the updated record in the list. Page reference: ![image](reference/workbook-home.png)
    - REQ-1-1-1 View and Open a Workbook (2 tests)
  - REQ-1-2 Workbook Creation and Naming
    Supports creating a blank workbook and changing the workbook name; both operations are initiated from visible workbook state points on the home page or editor page. After success, the workbook record on the home page and the editor title are updated consistently and remain so after refresh or reopening.
    - REQ-1-2-1 Create a Blank Workbook (1 tests)
    - REQ-1-2-2 Rename a Workbook (2 tests)
  - REQ-1-3 CSV Data Exchange
    Supports importing external CSV data completely as a workbook and exporting the current active worksheet as CSV. After a successful import, the Sheet1 editor page opens and continues to show the complete imported result after refresh or reopening; export reads only the current active worksheet and must not change workbook content or the current interface state.
    - REQ-1-3-1 Import CSV to Create a Workbook (4 tests)
    - REQ-1-3-2 Export the Current Worksheet as CSV (4 tests)
- REQ-2 Worksheets and Table Structure
  Supports managing multiple worksheets within one workbook and adjusting row and column structure. Each worksheet’s name, order, grid values, formulas, validation rules, filter views, and pivot table results are independent; switching worksheets or reopening the workbook must not display data from another worksheet. Page reference: ![image](reference/worksheet-overview.png)
  - REQ-2-1 Worksheet Lifecycle
    Supports creating, switching, renaming, and deleting worksheets while ensuring that each worksheet’s grid, formulas, validation behavior, filter views, pivot-table field selections, and results remain independent and persist after reopening. The worksheet tab bar displays worksheet order and active state after the most recent successful operation and provides a button with the accessible name "Add worksheet". Each worksheet tab provides a button with the accessible name "Worksheet options for <worksheet name>"; clicking it opens a menu whose commands use the ARIA menuitem role. Page reference: ![image](reference/worksheet-lifecycle.png)
    - REQ-2-1-1 Add a Worksheet (2 tests)
    - REQ-2-1-2 Switch Worksheets (5 tests)
    - REQ-2-1-3 Rename a Worksheet (3 tests)
    - REQ-2-1-4 Delete a Worksheet (4 tests)
  - REQ-2-2 Row and Column Structure Management
    Supports inserting and deleting rows and columns in the current active worksheet. After an operation, grid values, formula bar, filter views, validation behavior, and pivot refresh results remain consistent while other worksheets remain unchanged; the structure persists after refresh or reopening. Row numbers use the ARIA rowheader role with the decimal row number as the accessible name; column headers use the ARIA columnheader role with the column letter as the accessible name. Right-clicking a row number or column header opens a menu whose commands use the ARIA menuitem role.
    - REQ-2-2-1 Insert and Delete Rows (5 tests)
    - REQ-2-2-2 Insert and Delete Columns (5 tests)
- REQ-3 Cell and Range Editing
  Supports data entry, bulk paste, copy and cut, and undo and redo for cells and contiguous ranges in the current active worksheet. Each operation either completely updates the target grid, formula results, and related validation behavior and persists after refresh, or displays an error while the current and other worksheets continue to show the pre-operation state.
  - REQ-3-1 Direct Data Entry
    Supports entering data through the current worksheet grid, the text box labeled "Formula bar", or the external clipboard. The grid, formula bar, and selection state must show consistent content for the same cell; ordinary values and original formulas persist after refresh. Double-clicking a grid cell displays an inline text box with the accessible name "Edit <cell coordinate>".
    - REQ-3-1-1 Edit a Cell Through the Grid or Formula Bar (4 tests)
    - REQ-3-1-2 Paste Two-Dimensional Table Data (5 tests)
    - REQ-3-1-3 Select a Rectangular Cell Range (2 tests)
  - REQ-3-2 Range Transfer and Operation Recovery
    Supports transferring data between ranges in the current active worksheet and using undo and redo to restore grid values, formulas, rule ranges, and row/column structure. The visible state after each undo or redo persists after refresh.
    - REQ-3-2-1 Copy, Cut, and Paste Cell Ranges (4 tests)
    - REQ-3-2-2 Undo and Redo Recent Operations (7 tests)
- REQ-4 Formula Calculation
  Supports basic formula calculation, relative and absolute references, dependency recalculation, and error handling within the current active worksheet. The grid displays formula results or errors, while the formula bar displays the expression submitted by the user; copy, paste, row/column changes, and source-value edits follow the same reference-adjustment and recalculation rules. After reopening the workbook, formula expressions and correct results calculated from the current source values remain visible.
  - REQ-4-1 Formula Input and Functions
    Supports entering basic expressions and aggregate functions through the grid and "Formula bar" from REQ-3-1-1 and copying formulas through REQ-3-2-1. The formula bar always displays the original formula, the grid displays results consistent with the current source data, and both persist after refresh.
    - REQ-4-1-1 Calculate Basic Expressions and Aggregate Functions (5 tests)
    - REQ-4-1-2 Copy Formulas and Adjust Relative References (2 tests)
  - REQ-4-2 Dependency Updates and Error Handling
    Supports dependency recalculation after source data changes and isolation of formula errors. After REQ-3 value edits, pastes, and moves or REQ-2 row/column changes, all affected formulas display results consistent with the current source data; one erroneous formula does not affect unrelated cells.
    - REQ-4-2-1 Recalculate Dependent Formulas After Source Data Changes (3 tests)
    - REQ-4-2-2 Display and Fix Formula Errors (5 tests)
- REQ-5 Data Organization and Analysis
  Supports sorting, filtering, validation, and pivot-table summarization for data in the current active worksheet. After refresh or reopening, sort order, filter views, validation behavior, and pivot results persist; other worksheets are unaffected. Sorting changes the row order in the grid, filtering changes only visibility, validation constrains subsequent input, and pivot tables read source ranges without modifying source data. The editor toolbar provides a button with the accessible name "Data"; clicking it opens a menu whose commands use the ARIA menuitem role. Options in named combo boxes use the ARIA option role and their visible names.
  - REQ-5-1 Sorting and Filtering
    Supports sorting a selected rectangular range in the current worksheet by column and filtering it by value or condition. Sorting and filtering apply only to the range selected by the user and do not expand to adjacent data or other worksheets; the same order and visible rows persist after refresh.
    - REQ-5-1-1 Sort a Data Range by a Specified Column (6 tests)
    - REQ-5-1-2 Filter Rows by Value or Condition (5 tests)
  - REQ-5-2 Data Validation
    Supports configuring dropdown or numeric validation for ranges in the current active worksheet. The same rules are enforced when writing through the grid, formula bar, paste, or range move; after row or column changes, dropdown buttons and numeric limits move with the originally constrained cells. Rules remain active after refresh and existing valid values are preserved.
    - REQ-5-2-1 Set Dropdown or Numeric Validation for a Range (6 tests)
  - REQ-5-3 Basic Pivot Summarization
    Supports creating a basic pivot table from a data range in the current worksheet. Pivot results reside in a separate worksheet and only read source data; when switching back to the source worksheet, original values and order remain unchanged, and pivot results persist after refresh or reopening.
    - REQ-5-3-1 Create and Refresh a Basic Pivot Table (9 tests)

name: web-ui-basics
description: Rules every web UI follows: role and accessible-name uniqueness, values in their own elements, signed-in username display, headings, search highlighting, navigation that renders before data, URLs and API caching. Load before building any UI.
---
- Each named control has exactly the role and accessible name the requirement states, and no other visible element of that role in the view has a name containing it (no `Save draft` button beside `Save`).
- A required link, button, heading, label, badge or message appears once per page. A status or summary sentence (a count, a diff summary, "closed this issue") is stated in one element only, not repeated in per-item headers or activity lines: tests look such text up by substring or pattern and need exactly one match.
- A value a user looks for (a username, a team name) appears once per page, also as part of other text: a row button whose name includes the row's value shows short text (`Remove`, `⋯`) and carries the full name in `aria-label`.
- An open form or picker does not repeat a name already on the page: hide its opener while it is open, and name its own search field differently from the page's search.
- One click opens one editor. Each `<label>` text maps to one control; icon-only buttons have `aria-label`. Use exactly the control kind the requirement names.
- An entity page's `<h1>` is the entity's exact name or identifier; a display name goes in a separate paragraph; no other heading repeats the h1 text.
- A value inside a sentence (username, status, path, count) is the full text of its own element: `Assigned to <span>ann</span>, status <span>Open</span>`.
- User-entered text shows exactly as entered, before and after reload.
- Search matches are in `<mark>` in results and on the opened target; the target link carries the query (`?q=…`) so the highlighting survives reload.
- After sign-in the username appears once per page, as the full text of one element in the account menu button: no avatar initial, no "Signed in as" prefix, any arrow `aria-hidden`.
- A page's navigation (header, tabs, sidebar links, owner/admin action buttons) is in the DOM on the first render after the URL changes: derive it from the URL and the signed-in session, never wait for the page's data request; only lists and details wait. Route changes render synchronously (no transitions), and data already fetched renders at once on return. In-app links are plain `<a href>` elements, never react-router `<Link>`/`<NavLink>`/`navigate()` (client routing shows the next page before its data, so data-dependent links and owner-only buttons are missing when a test looks for them). A page starts its data request at mount, together with the session request, never after it; an auth guard does not delay it.
- Signed out, the header of every page, the sign-in and sign-up pages included, has the "Sign in" link.
- A page that needs a session, opened without one (directly, on reload, or by browser Back after sign-out), shows only a sign-in prompt and the "Sign in" link, none of its own headings or content. Only a page whose own action just ended the session keeps showing its content and result until the user navigates away.
- Every URL works on direct open and reload; unknown paths render home.
- `Cache-Control: no-store` on every `/api` response.

=== .agent/skills/data-and-persistence/SKILL.md
---
name: data-and-persistence
description: Saving every change durably and in order, surviving a reload right after an action, last-updated times, undo/redo history and filters in URLs. Load before designing the server data model or building saving, reload, undo/redo or list filters.
---
- An action is durable once the UI shows it: save the whole document on every change at once (PUT, `keepalive`, no debounce); the server handles one document's requests strictly in arrival order.
- Keep unanswered saves of every document in sessionStorage; re-send all before any page's first read, list pages included; a revision number lets the server drop stale copies.
- Set `updatedAt` on the client at each content change and store exactly that value, so every page shows the same time. UI state (selection, active tab) persists without bumping it.
- Undo/redo history is in memory per open document, empty after reload (Undo disabled); a new change clears Redo.
- List filters live in the query string (`?state=open&q=…`); switching a branch or similar view navigates to its URL.
=== .agent/skills/forms-and-dialogs/SKILL.md
---
name: forms-and-dialogs
description: Form validation, error display and clearing, refused writes, and dialog behaviour. Load before building any form, inline editor, error message or dialog.
---
- Validate every field on submit; show all errors together. Client-side checks never stop the server-side ones: submit even when a field is empty or invalid, and show every error together (required, format and already-exists). On error the form stays open with the typed value; the input gets `aria-invalid="true"` and `aria-describedby`/`aria-errormessage` to the error. While an edit form is open, the page heading keeps the stored value, also next to an error.
- An error stays until the next successful content change; a click, selection or tab switch does not clear it.
- A write refused by validation shows the message, closes any inline editor, keeps the old value displayed.

- Dialog: `role="dialog"` named by its `<h2>`; focus the first field; Escape closes; an outside click closes it. A confirmation dialog has one confirm button.

name: grids
description: Rendering, hiding filtered rows, focus, drag selection and keys in data grids and large tables. Load before building a grid, a large table, row filtering or any keyboard-driven widget.
---

- A keyboard-driven widget sits in a `div tabIndex=-1` focused on mousedown, so keys and paste reach it.

- A right-click inside the selection keeps it; context-menu commands act on the whole selection.
- Imported file content is stored as its original text (a field starting with `=` stays text); only typed input is interpreted.

- Undo/redo shortcuts are ignored while a text field has focus.
=== .agent/skills/menus-and-selects/SKILL.md
---
name: menus-and-selects
description: Markup for menus, ARIA comboboxes and option pickers. Load before building any menu, combobox or picker.
---

# GitHub - Stage 3
This product is a simplified GitHub collaboration platform. Unless an atomic requirement explicitly allows more than one role, every quoted user-interface name is the exact English accessible name of the control; the role, scope, and observable-state rules stated by each atomic requirement are authoritative. Values described as existing accounts, organizations, teams, repositories, branches, files, commits, issues, milestones, pull requests, reviews, and permission relationships are predefined seed data. The application must provision those records before the corresponding scenario and supply each account through an isolated browser session; they are not extra features that a participant must expose through a private API. Generated names may contain a unique suffix, but their role, ownership, visibility, and relationships are exactly those stated in the atomic requirement. Every atomic requirement remains enabled even when seed configuration is incomplete. Organization Owner, repository Admin, Read, Triage, Write, Maintain, and Admin permissions follow the operation-specific rules in the requirements below; these roles are not an automatic cumulative ladder. Real-time collaboration, Actions, Packages, Wiki, project boards, notification delivery, and external Git remote protocols are outside the scope of this product.

- REQ-5 Work Planning and Issue Management
  An issue is a persistent work item within a repository used to record pending work, a defect, or a discussion topic; it is not a code file or PR. The Issues page is the list page in repository navigation; each row displays the issue number, title, Open/Closed status, author, and labels, and clicking the number or title opens the issue detail page. At the top of the detail page are the title and status; the right side displays Assignees, Labels, and Milestone metadata in order; the main area displays the description, comments, and activity timeline. The “activity timeline” is an append-only history that records creation, edits, comments, assignment, labels, milestone, and status changes in chronological order. A label is a pre-existing colored classification name in the current repository; a milestone is a pre-existing goal-classification item in the current repository that may be associated with multiple issues or PRs but does not change their content or status. Write, Maintain, and Admin may create issues, edit titles/descriptions, and comment; Triage, Maintain, and Admin may assign participants, apply labels, set milestones, and close or reopen issues; Read may only view. Every operation is performed around a unique issue number within the repository, and the detail page and list display the same persisted data; after refresh, re-login, or opening from another account with view permission, the same record is still read. For issue operations, the explicit role lists in this module define eligibility per operation rather than an implicit cumulative grant from a role's name; Write can create, edit, and comment but cannot assign, label, set milestones, or change status. Organization Owners act with Admin permission. Read-only seed scenarios provide a public repository's visible Issues entry, distinct Open and Closed issues with known titles, and an issue entry with known title, description, metadata, and discussion. Mutation scenarios provide isolated issues for successful editing, invalid-title editing with a known original title, commenting, comment validation, assignment, labels, milestone, and closing; their initial states must not be changed by another scenario. The author and commenter accounts have Write or higher permission; the editor used for both content and metadata operations has Maintain or Admin permission. A separate viewer has Read permission on a protected issue. All authenticated scenarios use the home-page “Sign in” link, fields labeled “Username or email” and “Password”, and the “Sign in” button, after which the signed-in username is visible. Named controls below are unique on the active page unless a narrower scope is stated; detail pages and reloads must work independently of earlier list navigation.
  - REQ-5-1 Issue Discovery and Details
    The Issues list page displays the persisted work items for the current repository. Status and keyword filters change only the rows displayed in the browser and do not create, update, or delete issues. Each issue row identifies a repository-scoped issue and may display its number, title, Open/Closed status, author, labels, and update time. The issue detail page is the complete read view of one issue: it displays the issue number, title, status, saved description, metadata such as assignees, labels, and milestone, and discussion or activity records. Users with repository-view permission may read this information; editing and other mutation controls are governed by the corresponding role requirements. This feature builds on the public repository overview provided by REQ-3-3 (View a Public Repository Overview) and keeps list and detail views consistent after navigation or reload.
    - REQ-5-1-1 List and Filter Repository Issues (2 tests)
    - REQ-5-1-2 View an Issue and Its Discussion (3 tests)
  - REQ-5-2 Issue Creation and Discussion
    Supports creating issues in the current repository, editing titles and descriptions, and appending discussion comments. An issue title contains 1-256 non-empty characters after trimming leading and trailing whitespace; the description may be empty and is at most 65536 characters; a comment contains 1-65536 non-empty characters after trimming leading and trailing whitespace. A successful creation receives a unique repository-scoped number and Open status; editing changes only the selected field of the target issue; comments are appended as independent discussion records with their author and timestamp. Required-field validation and persistence failures must leave the affected issue or discussion unchanged. Each scenario supplies its own authenticated account and issue context, so it does not require a previous scenario to run.
    - REQ-5-2-1 Create a Repository Issue (2 tests)
    - REQ-5-2-2 Edit an Issue Title and Description (2 tests)
    - REQ-5-2-3 Comment on an Issue Discussion (2 tests)
  - REQ-5-3 Issue Metadata and Classification
    An assignee is a repository member associated with an issue; a label is a repository-scoped classification; and a milestone is a repository-scoped planning target. These metadata relationships do not change repository permission. Users with Triage, Maintain, or Admin permission may modify them, while other users may view the saved metadata only. Selecting an available option saves the relationship immediately; reload displays the saved state. Each scenario provisions its own account, target issue, and selectable repository-scoped metadata.
    - REQ-5-3-1 Assign or Unassign Issue Participants (1 tests)
    - REQ-5-3-2 Apply Labels to an Issue (1 tests)
    - REQ-5-3-3 Assign Issues and Pull Requests to a Milestone (1 tests)
  - REQ-5-4 Close or Reopen an Issue (2 tests)
- REQ-6 Change Review and Merge Control
  A pull request (PR) is a persistent proposal to “merge code changes from the compare branch into the base branch”; it is not a branch, commit, or issue. The Pull requests page lists the current repository's PR number, title, author, source/target branches, and status; “New pull request” first opens the comparison page, where the user selects base (the target branch that receives the changes) and compare (the source branch that provides the changes) and inspects the diff. On the PR detail page, Conversation displays the title, description, ordinary comments, activities, and review summary; Commits displays commits on the compare branch relative to base; Files changed displays per-file, per-line differences; Checks displays check status for the PR's current compare commit. A PR's persisted status may only be Draft, Open, Closed, or Merged — normal creation produces Open, draft creation produces Draft, and the author or Maintain/Admin may mark a Draft as Ready for review to transition it to Open; the author or Maintain/Admin may transition an unmerged Open or Draft PR to Closed and may transition Closed back to Open; Merged is terminal and cannot be closed or reopened. Write, Maintain, and Admin may add inline comments and submit reviews, the author or Maintain/Admin may request reviewers, and only Maintain, Admin, or organization Owner may merge. Each PR stores a repository-scoped number, source/target branches, creation-time and current compare commits, creation-time base commit, title, description, author, status, and activity records. When the compare branch receives a new commit, the system updates the current compare commit, marks all existing review decisions as stale while preserving them in the timeline, recalculates merge eligibility, and retains inline comments at their original commit and line position marked Outdated. Failure does not change branches or PR state. The following REQ-6 interaction contracts use English accessible names and apply to direct navigation as well as navigation from a repository. Each named action, field, and navigation link is unique on its active page unless explicitly repeated per changed line or reviewer. PR titles are headings whose accessible name is exactly the persisted title; list titles are links with that same exact name. Conversation, Commits, Files changed, and Checks are navigation links, even when visually styled as tabs. The current PR status is visible text. Signed-in scenarios begin with the unique Sign in link on the home page, labeled Username or email and Password fields, a Sign in button, and the account username visible after authentication; each role account has a username, verified email, and password. Visitor scenarios use public repositories and require no session. Seed records identify the corresponding pages, not to private implementation interfaces; role accounts, branches, PRs, and mutable state must be provisioned as distinct records for each stateful scenario; no scenario may rely on a mutation performed by an earlier scenario, and the complete seed set is present before the serial suite starts. Existing titles, usernames, paths, and branch names described below are supplied as seed values and must be displayed verbatim; generated PR titles and comments may carry a unique suffix.
  - REQ-6-1 Protect Branches with Review and Status-Check Requirements (3 tests)
  - REQ-6-2 Pull Request Discovery and Creation
    Supports listing pull requests, comparing source and target branches, and creating normal or draft PRs from a valid comparison. Public visitors may read PR lists; authenticated users with Write, Maintain, or Admin may create PRs. Normal PRs start Open, draft PRs start Draft, and an authorized draft author may mark a draft Ready for review. Each scenario provisions independent accounts, branches, PRs, and mutable state.
    - REQ-6-2-1 List and Filter Repository Pull Requests (3 tests)
    - REQ-6-2-2 Compare Branches Before Opening a Pull Request (2 tests)
    - REQ-6-2-3 Create a Pull Request from Comparison Results (2 tests)
    - REQ-6-2-4 Create a Draft Pull Request (2 tests)
  - REQ-6-3 Pull Request Review Workspace
    A pull request detail page provides read-only overview, Commits, and Files changed views for repository viewers. A non-author reviewer with Write, Maintain, or Admin permission can add line comments and submit review decisions on an Open PR. A line comment is anchored to the current changed code and is either published immediately or stored as a pending review comment. A review stores its reviewer, decision, optional summary, and current compare commit. Each scenario provisions independent PRs, account roles, changed files, and review state.
    - REQ-6-3-1 View Pull Request Overview and Commits (3 tests)
    - REQ-6-3-2 Inspect Changed Files and Aggregate Diff (1 tests)
    - REQ-6-3-3 Add Review Comments to Changed Code Lines (2 tests)
    - REQ-6-3-4 Submit a Pull Request Review (2 tests)
  - REQ-6-4 Request or Remove Pull Request Reviewers (1 tests)
  - REQ-6-5 Merge an Eligible Pull Request (2 tests)
  - REQ-6-6 Close or Reopen a Pull Request Without Merging (2 tests)
